CBY decision requires new domestic cash transfers to be executed through the unified transfer network, with stated exceptions/transitional arrangements for bank networks and licensed wallets/PSPs.

The World Bank-financed Yemen Financial Market Infrastructure and Inclusion Project (P180708), implemented by UNDP with CBY-Aden as primary beneficiary, became effective on 1 September 2025, after Board approval on 17 June 2025 and signing on 26 June 2025 (World Bank ISR for P180708, sequence 2 (8 April 2026), key dates and components). The report gives no separate start date.
Project component 'Development of Fast Payment Systems (FPS)', approved with the project on 17 June 2025 (World Bank ISR for P180708, sequence 2 (8 April 2026), key dates and components).

Project component 'Development of a Real Time Gross Settlement System and upgrading Core Banking for CBY Aden', approved with the project on 17 June 2025 (World Bank ISR for P180708, sequence 2 (8 April 2026), key dates and components).

Project component 'Supporting access and usage of the payment's infrastructure', approved with the project on 17 June 2025 (World Bank ISR for P180708, sequence 2 (8 April 2026), key dates and components); its results indicators are merchants accepting electronic payments, active bank and e-wallet accounts and agents. The UNDP description of an access-point database is not read here.
Unified network as main transfer channel
CBY reports adoption of the unified network as a main channel for financial transfers and discusses completion of integration among banks and financial service providers.

CBY records issuance/listing of regulatory instructions for financial consumer protection; issuance notice states a one-year maximum adjustment period for banks and other non-bank financial institutions.
National QR + e-wallet interconnection + FPS operator participation
CBY board approves a mandatory national QR standard, linking electronic wallets, and CBY participation as a main shareholder in the FPS operator company, with execution steps assigned.
Mobile e-money instructions for non-bank financial institutions
CBY issued instructions governing mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions under its supervision, including consumer-protection/complaint controls.
Signed amendment permits USD/SAR/AED e-money in addition to YER, restricts local-to-foreign conversion within scope, updates individual transaction/balance ceilings and takes effect from issuance.
CBY-supported official event / attributed operational statement
Digital-payment exhibition and unified-network activity signal

CBY news reports >9 e-wallets at the exhibition and attributes to the Director General of Payment Systems that 22 transfer networks were unified, >YER 251bn passed through the unified network in 2024 and all banks/e-wallets joined it.
Restructuring, capital increase and broader bank shareholder base
CBY reports a new phase for the Unified Money Network company after restructuring, capital increase and expansion of shareholders with banks joining.
Founding assembly of Yemen Payments and Clearing Company
CBY opens the founding assembly of YPCC with banks, financial institutions and development partners represented.
The newly elected YPCC board holds its first meeting and elects its chair/vice-chair.
July-2025 mission produced BOP/IIP statistics for 2014–2024 and strengthened source/compilation practice.
IMF D4D-II FY26 midyear implementation report

Regulatory Instructions for Financial Consumer Protection were issued as the formal framework; the issuance notice states a one-year maximum adjustment period for banks and other non-bank financial institutions.
Instrument existence, official date/title, stated purpose and announced adjustment period.
Full controlled legal-text extraction, current applicability/amendments/supersession and clause-level legal interpretation.
Official brochure states that a dedicated customer-protection department was created within Banking Supervision and that compliance with consumer-protection requirements is followed up.
Source-reported supervisory architecture and institutional responsibility.
Staffing, supervisory intensity, inspection frequency, sanctions and effectiveness are not measured.
The brochure identifies banking financial institutions and non-bank financial institutions as institutions subject to the financial-consumer-protection instructions.
Source-attributed coverage classes can be displayed.
Exact clause-level scope, exemptions and current legal applicability still require the controlled instruction text.

Providers should maintain clear complaint policies, multiple reporting channels, trained complaint staff, complaint validation/analysis, appropriate actions, professional response, transparency/continuous improvement, risk identification and appropriate compensation; providers should notify CBY if unable to settle within the specified time.
When a customer complaint is received
No administrative evidence that every provider has implemented these controls or that compensation/redress occurs consistently.
The source states a maximum of 10 business days to settle a consumer complaint from the date of complaint submission with the necessary attachments.
The source-reported provider-stage time window can be shown in a redress-path visual.
Observed resolution time, compliance rate and complaint outcome remain unknown.
For complaints requiring it, the settlement period may be extended for a similar period, with the consumer informed of the justification for the extension.
The source-reported extension rule and notification requirement.
No evidence on how often extensions are used or whether reasons are adequate.
A complaint may be escalated to CBY when no response is received from the financial service provider within the specified time or when the complainant is not satisfied with the provider's decision.
The source-attributed escalation triggers can be shown.
Actual accessibility, usage and success of escalation are not established.

The brochure states that escalation to CBY should be submitted within 14 business days from the end of the time framework specified for complaint settlement in the applicable instructions, using the prescribed form.
The source-reported escalation window can be displayed.
No controlled complaint volumes, rejection reasons, processing time or resolution outcomes at CBY stage.

A source-attributed principle map for the consumer-protection framework.

Full local custody and consolidated amendment/supersession register remain incomplete.
E-money is defined as electronically stored value issued against receipt of equivalent value, accepted as a means of payment, transferable among users and redeemable to cash at the same value.
A source-controlled definition of the regulated e-money object.
Does not identify current licensed issuers or active users.

The base instructions require consumer-protection controls including effective contact channels, clear customer agreements, transaction notifications, customer verification of beneficiary/value before completion and prompt complaint handling.
Consumer-protection obligations within the mobile e-money regime can be described source-by-source.
Compliance, complaint performance and enforcement remain unmeasured.
The base instructions state that complaint processing should not exceed 10 business days from notification and require a dedicated complaint register recording complaints and treatment actions.
Observed complaint count, compliance and resolution quality are open.
